newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia money market rate slips to 9.2 vs 11.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatia money market rate slips to 9.2 vs 11.6 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average money market rate slipped to 9.2 percent on Tuesday from 11.6 percent amid improved liquidity of the banking sector.
Dealers put daily trade at 43 million kuna, leaving an extra five million on the supply side. Rolled over loans made up roughly one third of the total settlements.
The call money rate fell back one percentage point to 8.0 percent.

The rate for fresh one-week interbank loans was 10 percent and banks rolled over old loans at 9.0 and 10.5 percent. The two-week loans were made at 12 percent, with rates for renewed deals ranging betweeen 11 and 14 percent.

The central bank stayed out of the foreign exchange market. It calculated its kuna midrates for Wednesday weaker at 6.2637 to the dollar and 3.5715 against the German mark. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
